rules.title: 14-day notice to quit for nonpayment of rent under a written lease; tenant right to cure
rules.requirement: To end a written lease for nonpayment of rent, the landlord must give the tenant 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenancy continues if the tenant pays all rent due, with interest and costs, by the day the answer is due in the eviction action. Courts must continue the hearing at least seven days when nonpayment was caused by government delay in rental or subsistence payments.
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice; cure by answer date
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential and other tenancies under a written lease in Massachusetts where the tenant has neglected or refused to pay rent due.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only to tenancies under a written lease where rent is unpaid. The hearing continuance applies only when nonpayment was caused by government delay in subsistence or rental payments.

rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease, unless the tenant, on or before the day the answer is due, in an action by the landlord to recover possession of the premises, pays or tenders to the landlord or to his attorney all rent then due, with interest and costs of suit.
rules.conflict_note: This is an eviction notice and cure procedure for nonpayment, not a just-cause requirement. Massachusetts has no statewide just-cause eviction law in this document. It is categorized under just_cause_eviction only as the closest eviction-protection category. The document gives no effective date.
